notes: 📅 The report card now knows what month it is. A ten-year seasonality study today (21.5 million day-changes, every ordinary ASX share) found exactly one calendar effect that passed every honesty test: the end-of-financial-year straddle. July is the band's strongest month — up in 10 of 11 years (and 11 of 11 across the rest of the market), unchanged across both halves of the decade — and June is its mirror, the tax-loss-selling month, −25bp/day since 2022. August carries a softer, remarkably era-stable tailwind; February–March a soft headwind; every other month honestly reads 'no reliable lean'. A new 📅 line beside the 🌡 tape banner states the current month's climate in one sentence, and the tooltip publishes the full twelve-month decade table with the caveats (only ~10 years per month; survivorship-biased store, so levels are ceilings). Climate, never a signal: it colours how you read the card and gates nothing — no grade, score or bot decision uses it.
